items.passage: Gdansk in late October smells of wet grass and diesel from the shipyards, and that is where Milena found me, sitting on the bench beside the soccer field my brothers used to rule every evening. She had known my parents since before I was born, and she still called me Ksenia the goalkeeper. Our house two streets away was empty except for one thing: the cracked leather ball my father had signed for each of us. I told Milena I would throw it out, because keeping it felt like refusing to leave. She said nothing. She kicked it once across the darkening grass and waited. I ran after it before I knew I had decided to, and somewhere near the far goal I understood that a thing could be carried forward without becoming a weight. We walked home under the floodlights, the ball under my arm.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show how a friend's gesture altered the narrator's view of keeping a family object
To explain why the narrator finally agreed to sell her family's house after many years
To recall the narrator's childhood rivalry with her brothers on the neighborhood field
To argue that old family friends often understand grief better than close relatives do
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 공을 간직하는 것이 떠나기를 거부하는 것 같다며 버리려 한다. 그러나 Milena가 말없이 공을 차 보내자 화자는 공을 쫓아가며 물건을 짐이 아니라 앞으로 가져갈 수 있는 것으로 깨닫는다. 두 장면을 연결하면 친구의 행동이 간직함에 대한 화자의 시각을 바꾸었다는 A가 글의 목적이다. B는 집 매각 결정이 언급되지 않고, C와 D는 지문의 일부 소재만 확대한 오답이다.

items.passage: "Finish the balcony rail before the monsoon," Lakshmi said on the first morning I came to work for her at the shuttered cinema outside Thrissur. I was seventeen, and she was the last carpenter in the district who still built everything by hand. When I asked who the rail was for, she said the owner had been promised it years ago. But the owner, visiting in June, could not recall any such promise; the theater would reopen with or without a rail. Lakshmi only nodded and handed me the plane. All summer we shaped teak while the empty seats watched us. Only later did I see that she had kept the promise for its own sake, and for mine. On the last day she let me, Kenji, the apprentice who had once rushed every joint, set the final peg.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how the narrator came to resent a master who hid her true reasons
To convey how a forgotten promise became a lesson in valuing work for itself
To explain how the off-season shaped the business choices of a small cinema owner
To recount the narrator's long struggle to master traditional carpentry by hand
items.explanation: 주인은 난간 약속을 기억하지 못하고 극장은 난간 없이도 다시 문을 열 수 있었지만, Lakshmi는 묵묵히 작업을 계속한다. 화자는 나중에 그녀가 약속을 그 자체와 자신을 위해 지켰음을 깨닫고, 서두르던 견습생이 마지막 쐐기를 박게 된다. 두 단서를 연결하면 잊힌 약속이 일 자체를 소중히 여기는 교훈이 되었다는 B가 요지다. A의 원망은 근거가 없고, C와 D는 배경이나 기술 습득만 부각한 오답이다.

items.passage: Three stops, eleven minutes: that was how long Bruno had to talk with his cousin Caio each morning before Caio stepped off near the weaving cooperative in Lisbon. Their grandmother's old loom house, left to both of them, now had a buyer, and Caio wanted to sign by Friday. Only last week Caio had complained that the cooperative had outgrown its single cramped room. Today Bruno said nothing about the offer. Instead he pulled the bus to the curb one stop early, beside the cooperative's back window, where Caio's apprentices were threading a loom that had once stood in their grandmother's front room. Caio looked at the loom, then at Bruno, who kept his eyes fixed on the mirror. Walk from here, Bruno said. The air is good this morning.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Bruno most likely stop the bus one stop early?
options: He wants to avoid an argument by letting Caio leave before the offer comes up.
He is following a new route rule that requires him to stop near the cooperative.
He hopes the sight of the loom will lead Caio to reconsider selling the house.
He wants Caio's apprentices to see that he supports the cooperative's work.
items.explanation: Caio는 집을 팔려 하지만 지난주 협동조합이 좁은 방 하나로는 부족하다고 불평했다. Bruno는 매각 이야기를 꺼내지 않고 할머니의 베틀이 보이는 창가에 버스를 세운다. 두 단서를 연결하면 Bruno는 베틀을 보여 주어 Caio가 집을 조합의 작업장으로 쓸 가능성을 떠올리고 매각을 재고하길 바란다는 C가 맞다. A는 그럴듯하지만 Bruno는 대화를 피하기보다 메시지를 전하고 있고, B와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Years later, Karim would still describe the kitchen of that Bologna trattoria as a ship's galley: narrow, brass-railed, every pot hung where the sway of a sea might have flung it. He had come only to deliver flour. But he lingered in the doorway, watching Assunta correct her new daughter-in-law's pasta for the third time: too thick, too dry, too hurried. The bride said nothing and rolled the dough again. To the family at the long table outside, the two women looked like a perfectly matched pair. Karim saw instead that the young woman's hands were shaking, and that Assunta, without a word, slid the flour bin closer to her each time she spoke. Every correction was a rope thrown, not a blow. He left the sacks by the stove and never mentioned it to anyone.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a rope thrown, not a blow” most nearly suggests that Assunta's corrections are
options: a quiet form of support rather than an attack.
a test meant to push the bride out of the kitchen.
a habit she learned while working aboard a ship.
a public display meant for the family outside.
items.explanation: Karim은 신부의 손이 떨리는 것과, Assunta가 지적할 때마다 말없이 밀가루 통을 신부 쪽으로 밀어 주는 것을 본다. 이 두 장면이 비유와 연결되어, 지적이 공격이 아니라 물에 빠진 사람에게 던지는 밧줄 같은 도움임을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 지적의 표면만 본 오해이고, C는 배의 주방 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었으며, D는 가족이 이 장면을 제대로 보지 못한다는 점과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Seeds do not argue. Nalani had said this for thirty years, sorting packets at the cooperative in upcountry Maui while her daughter Fatma grew up beneath the drying racks. Now Fatma sat across the sorting table with a wedding list in one hand and, in the other, a letter offering her fiancé a post in Edinburgh. She expected her mother to object. Nalani only kept labeling: taro, sweet potato, a squash with no English name. Then she pressed one envelope into Fatma's palm. A seed, she said, is a whole garden folded small enough to travel. Fatma turned it over and recognized her grandmother's handwriting on the flap. For the first time that afternoon, the list in her other hand seemed less like a farewell than a packing note.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a whole garden folded small enough to travel” most nearly suggests that
options: the cooperative plans to ship its seed collection to Scotland.
what Fatma has inherited can be carried into a new life elsewhere.
Nalani believes Fatma's wedding plans are too small and hurried.
gardens in unfamiliar places rarely thrive without local seeds.
items.explanation: Fatma는 에든버러로 떠나는 문제에 어머니가 반대할 것이라 예상하지만, Nalani는 할머니의 글씨가 적힌 씨앗 봉투를 건넨다. 그 뒤 결혼 목록이 작별이 아니라 짐 목록처럼 느껴졌다는 변화가 이어진다. 두 단서를 종합하면 이 비유는 물려받은 것을 낯선 곳의 새 삶으로 가져갈 수 있다는 뜻이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽은 것이고, C와 D는 지문의 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Once, at the hour the ward lights dim to amber,
Mingyu asked me for a map of the old creek
that cut through his part of Shanghai before the city paved it.
I am Yuxuan, a nurse; I keep charts, not maps,
but I drew what he described on the back of one:
a footbridge, a willow, the dry stones he crossed in August
when the water had gone somewhere else to sleep.
He traced it with a finger that no longer trusted itself.
That is the way, he said, and closed his eyes.
I folded the chart into his pocket.
Every night since, I have walked a riverbed of linoleum,
listening for the water to come home.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a riverbed of linoleum” most nearly suggests that the speaker
options: resents the hospital for replacing the creek that once ran there.
has begun to sleepwalk through the ward during her night shifts.
still carries the patient's remembered route through her rounds.
believes the patient's map was too inaccurate to be followed.
items.explanation: 화자는 환자 Mingyu가 묘사한 마른 개울길을 차트 뒷면에 그려 주었고, 환자는 그것이 길이라고 말한 뒤 눈을 감는다. 이후 화자는 매일 밤 병동 바닥을 마른 강바닥처럼 걸으며 물이 돌아오기를 기다린다. 두 부분을 연결하면 이 비유는 화자가 환자의 기억 속 길을 일상의 순회 속에 계속 품고 다닌다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 원망의 근거가 없고, B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었으며, D는 지문 내용과 반대된다.

items.passage: By the third week of rehearsals, I had stopped counting the hems. Haruo, who took me on as his only apprentice the winter I arrived in Hokkaido, was dressing the whole cast of the town's lake festival play, and he sewed the way some people pray, on the dock at dawn where the light was honest. I was Moshe, the clumsy foreigner who kept dropping pins between the boards. One morning he held up a cloak I had finished and turned it slowly against the lake. Every stitch shows, he said, and I braced myself. Then he added that a costume should be a confession, not a disguise: the audience ought to see the hands that made it. I looked again. My uneven seams caught the light like ripples, and he hung the cloak beside his own.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a confession, not a disguise” most nearly suggests that Haruo believes a costume should
options: hide the actor so completely that the audience forgets who he is.
be sewn quickly enough to be ready before the final rehearsal.
expose an apprentice's mistakes so that he will learn from them.
openly display the work of its makers instead of hiding it.
items.explanation: Haruo는 바늘땀이 다 보인다고 말한 직후 관객이 옷을 만든 손을 볼 수 있어야 한다고 덧붙인다. 또 화자의 고르지 않은 솔기가 빛을 받는 모습을 보고 그 망토를 자기 작품 옆에 건다. 두 단서를 연결하면 의상은 만든 사람의 노동을 숨기지 말고 드러내야 한다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. C는 그럴듯하지만 Haruo는 실수를 꾸짖는 것이 아니라 인정하고 있으며, A와 B는 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Two rules governed the salt flat behind the house I rented outside Port of Spain: never walk on a pan that is still drying, and never rake against the wind. Shanice, my landlord, taught me both in my first month there, though I had only asked her about the leaking roof. She was the last person on that stretch of coast who still harvested salt by hand, and her own children had moved to offices in the city. She called me Alisha-girl, as if I were a niece rather than a tenant. Each evening she handed me the long wooden rake and corrected my wrist without comment. I assumed she simply wanted cheap help. Then, the summer she grew too ill to stand in the heat, she gave me the rake for good and called it the only lease she had ever meant. I rented that house eleven more years and never asked about the roof again.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the only lease she had ever meant” most nearly suggests that Shanice viewed
options: teaching her craft as the true bond between her and the narrator.
the rental contract as a legal burden she wished to end quickly.
the rake as payment owed to her for many years of unpaid rent.
her illness as a reason to sell the salt flat to the narrator.
items.explanation: Shanice는 자녀들이 도시로 떠난 뒤 해안에서 손으로 소금을 거두는 마지막 사람이며, 세입자인 화자를 조카처럼 부르며 매일 기술을 가르친다. 병들어 일을 못 하게 되자 갈퀴를 넘겨주며 이것이 자신이 진심으로 맺은 유일한 계약이라고 말한다. 두 단서를 종합하면 기술을 물려주는 일이 두 사람 사이의 진짜 약속이었다는 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 임대 계약이나 금전 관계를 문자 그대로 해석한 오답이다.

items.passage: Aster had spent the week at the monastery guesthouse in Addis Ababa refusing everything her stepmother offered: tea, the window seat, an explanation of why they had come. Then, looking for a pen, she opened the desk drawer and found a bundle of letters in Imani's handwriting, all addressed to Aster's late father and all dated before the wedding. She expected to find something she could use against Imani. Instead the letters asked, again and again, whether a girl who had lost her mother would ever forgive a stranger for moving into the house. Aster read them twice. When Imani came in with the evening tea, Aster did not ______ it, as she had every night that week; she took the cup and moved over to make room on the bed.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: notice
refuse
prepare
examine
items.explanation: 첫 문장에서 Aster는 일주일 내내 차를 포함해 새어머니가 권하는 모든 것을 거절했다고 나온다. 빈칸 뒤의 '그 주 매일 밤 그랬듯이'라는 표현과 이번에는 잔을 받아 들었다는 대조를 연결하면 빈칸에는 거절하다는 뜻이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 그럴듯해 보이지만 Aster가 차를 알아채지 못했다는 근거가 없고, C와 D는 문맥상 매일 밤 하던 행동과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: When the shop closed at six, the rule in Aiko's family was that no one touched the workbench but her. For forty years the neighbors in Kyoto had brought their radios to that bench, and for most of those years her grandson Sota had watched from the doorway, forbidden even to hold a screwdriver. Everyone obeyed, though no one could say why. So Sota was startled, one rainy evening, when Aiko pushed a dead transistor radio across the bench toward him and stepped back. She did not explain herself; she simply waited. The rule had not been announced as broken, but her silence made it clear that it had been ______: she would not lift it publicly, yet she would no longer enforce it.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: strengthened
forgotten
suspended
misunderstood
items.explanation: 규칙이 깨졌다고 공표되지는 않았지만 Aiko는 직접 라디오를 Sota에게 밀어 주며 의도적으로 기다린다. 콜론 뒤의 설명은 규칙을 공식적으로 없애지는 않되 더 이상 집행하지 않겠다는 뜻이므로, 일시적으로 효력을 멈춘다는 C가 가장 정확하다. B는 그럴듯하지만 Aiko의 행동은 잊어버린 것이 아니라 의도적인 선택이다. A와 D는 문맥의 방향과 반대되거나 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Glasgow rain on the barbershop glass,
and Beatriz, who keeps the window boxes,
sweeping petals the new owner never notices.
Caoimhe has asked her, twice, about the name
scraped from the old sign above the door.
Twice Beatriz has talked of geraniums instead,
of frost, of how late the bulbs came up this year.
She knew the man whose name it was,
knows where he went and why he must not be found,
and her talk of flowers is not forgetfulness
but a ______ silence, a fence of green
she tends so no one will step through.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: careless
hostile
puzzled
protective
items.explanation: Beatriz는 간판 속 이름의 주인이 어디로 왜 갔는지 알면서도 그가 발견되어서는 안 된다는 이유로 꽃 이야기로 질문을 피한다. 빈칸 뒤의 '아무도 넘어오지 못하게 가꾸는 초록 울타리'라는 비유도 누군가를 지키는 침묵을 가리킨다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 '망각이 아니다'라는 표현과 충돌하고, B는 그럴듯하지만 Beatriz가 새 주인에게 적대적이라는 근거가 없으며, C는 그녀가 모든 사정을 안다는 점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: After the funeral, my son Budi refused to leave the cemetery gate in Lagos until he had read every name on its iron plaque. I am Despina, and I had married into a family that did not discuss its past. My husband stood beside us, impatient, while Budi traced one name with his thumb: the name my husband had been given at birth and had dropped at nineteen. Budi asked why no one used it anymore. My husband said it no longer mattered. But Budi, who at twelve had never once let a question go, repeated it at dinner, at breakfast, and on the drive to school. By the end of the week my husband's answers had become less dismissive and more ______, as if he were testing how much of the old name he could bear to say aloud.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: tentative
rehearsed
impatient
cheerful
items.explanation: 남편은 처음에 그 이름이 중요하지 않다고 일축했지만, 아들의 반복된 질문 끝에 대답이 덜 무시하는 쪽으로 바뀐다. 빈칸 뒤의 '옛 이름을 얼마나 소리 내어 말할 수 있는지 시험하듯'이라는 표현은 조심스럽고 머뭇거리는 태도를 가리키므로 A가 정답이다. C는 앞부분의 남편 모습과 맞아 그럴듯하지만 '덜 무시하는'과의 대조에 어긋난다. B와 D는 시험하듯 조심스럽게 말한다는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I was nine the summer Isaiah let me sweep his stall at the Saturday market outside Clarksdale, and the first lesson I learned there was about Lucius. Every week Lucius admired the cane-bottom chairs Isaiah wove, running his palm along the seats and praising the tight weave to anyone within earshot. Every week he left without buying one. I asked Isaiah why he kept setting out his best chair for a man who never paid. He said praise was a kind of rent, too small to live on but too honest to refuse. Still, I noticed that he never lowered his price for Lucius, and he never stopped weaving. His patience was not ______; it was a decision he renewed each Saturday morning.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: genuine
passive
deliberate
limited
items.explanation: Isaiah는 값을 깎지 않으면서도 매주 가장 좋은 의자를 내놓고 계속 의자를 짠다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그의 인내는 매주 토요일 새로 내리는 결정이라고 설명되므로, 빈칸에는 그 반대인 수동적이라는 뜻이 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. C는 오히려 세미콜론 뒤 내용과 같은 의미라 '아니다'와 결합하면 모순이 되고, A와 D도 문맥의 대조 구조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: On Tuesdays at four, Matheus brought the pharmacy order to the hospital waiting room in Porto Alegre, and on Tuesdays at four Putri was already there, folding the free newspapers into neat stacks for the volunteers. She had started the chore while her husband was a patient upstairs; she kept at it, she told Matheus briskly, only because the stacks were always a mess and someone had to fix them. He usually helped with the last pile before running to his next delivery. This week he arrived to find the papers already folded and Putri sitting with her hands empty in her lap. The volunteers had hired a cleaner, she said. Then, after a pause, she asked whether he might sit a moment anyway, since she no longer knew what to do with four o'clock.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from brisk practicality to a quiet admission of loneliness.
It moves from cheerful nostalgia to open anger at the volunteers.
It moves from anxious worry about a patient to calm, settled relief.
It moves from playful teasing to stiff, formal politeness toward Matheus.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Putri는 신문 접기를 누군가 해야 할 일일 뿐이라고 사무적으로 말한다. 그러나 일이 사라지자 빈손으로 앉아 있다가 네 시를 어떻게 보내야 할지 모르겠다며 잠시 앉아 달라고 부탁한다. 두 장면을 연결하면 실용적인 어조가 조용한 외로움의 고백으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 환자 걱정, D의 농담은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage: When Soren came home to the beekeeper's yard in Manila, he went straight to the hive their father had built, the one whose roof had split in the typhoon two years before. Kaya watched from the porch as he measured, sawed, and nailed with the energy of a man following orders, whistling and announcing every step: new cedar, tighter joints, good as before. She brought him water and laughed when a bee settled in his hair. By late afternoon the roof was whole. Soren stood back to admire it, and the whistling stopped. The bees had moved long ago to a hollow in the mango tree, and none of them came near the box. He set the hammer down very carefully, as though it might break, and asked Kaya, without turning, how long they had been gone.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from tense suspicion between siblings to relieved good cheer.
It moves from bustling confidence to a subdued, sorrowful recognition.
It moves from mournful reflection on the past to firm optimism.
It moves from playful rivalry to open resentment of his sister.
items.explanation: 앞부분의 Soren은 휘파람을 불며 작업 단계를 하나하나 외치는 자신감 넘치는 모습이다. 그러나 지붕을 다 고친 뒤 벌들이 오래전에 떠났다는 사실을 깨닫자 휘파람이 멈추고 망치를 조심스럽게 내려놓으며 조용히 묻는다. 두 장면의 대비는 분주한 자신감에서 가라앉은 슬픈 깨달음으로의 전환을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 전환 방향이 반대이고, D의 원망은 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Dayoung had not spoken to me for two years when she mailed me a swimsuit, plain navy and one size too large. I read it as an insult, a remark on the weight I had gained after my divorce, and I left it in its box. Last month, in Busan for our aunt's birthday, I went alone to the salt-water pool by the breakwater where we had swum as girls. Dongsik, the attendant who had worked there since we were children, recognized me at once. He said my sister came every Sunday and always asked whether I had been in. Then he pointed to the lockers. Hers still bore a tag with both our names, written in the round letters of a ten-year-old. I stood a long time in the wet air, thinking of the navy suit, bought large the way our mother always bought clothes for girls she expected to grow.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from nostalgic warmth to bitter disappointment in a sister.
It moves from detached humor to anxious urgency about a reunion.
It moves from wounded suspicion to softened, regretful understanding.
It moves from calm curiosity to outright joy at meeting a sister.
items.explanation: 처음에 화자는 큰 수영복을 체중에 대한 모욕으로 받아들이고 상자에 넣어 둔다. 그러나 수영장에서 언니가 매주 자신을 찾았다는 말과 두 사람의 이름이 적힌 사물함을 본 뒤, 수영복을 어머니가 자랄 아이에게 옷을 사 주던 방식과 연결한다. 이 흐름은 상처받은 의심에서 누그러진 후회 섞인 이해로의 전환이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 방향이 반대이고, B와 D는 지문에 없는 감정이다.

items.passage: Although the night-shift pharmacy on Calle Zanja sold only aspirin and cough syrup after midnight, Wenhua sat there every night that week, because its phone was the only one on the block that still worked. His daughter sat beside him with a dictionary, since the call would come from the embassy in English. Booker, the pharmacist, pretended not to notice them and kept the radio low. For hours nothing happened: the fan turned, a taxi driver bought antacid, Wenhua smoothed the same receipt over and over. At four in the morning the phone rang. His daughter listened, said yes three times, and hung up. Before she could translate, Wenhua read her face and began to laugh, and Booker, who had understood nothing, turned the radio all the way up.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It introduces a conflict between a father and daughter and then shows a stranger resolving it.
It describes a pharmacy's nightly routine and then explains why that routine is about to end.
It recounts a phone call in detail and then reflects on its lasting effects on a family.
It depicts a long, uneventful wait and then shifts to the moment the news arrives.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 아버지와 딸이 대사관의 전화를 기다리며 아무 일도 일어나지 않는 긴 밤을 묘사한다. 새벽 네 시에 전화가 울리면서 초점은 소식이 도착하는 순간과 그에 대한 반응으로 옮겨 간다. 따라서 긴 기다림에서 소식 도착으로 이동하는 D가 구조를 정확히 설명한다. A의 부녀 갈등과 B의 일과 종료는 근거가 없고, C는 통화 내용이나 장기적 결과를 다루지 않는다는 점에서 틀리다.

items.passage: Chengdu's old Number Seven Middle School gymnasium was coming down in the spring, and Weiqi had been sent to return a box his late grandfather had left there for Zhiming, the retired coach. Inside lay a pair of hand-stitched leather gymnastics grips. Weiqi expected gratitude. Instead Zhiming pushed the box back across the scorer's table. Your grandfather made these for me in 1979, he said, the week I broke my wrist and he took my place at the provincial meet. I returned them then, too. He looked up at the rafters, where the old rings still hung. He won that meet wearing them. I always thought they belonged to the one who used them. Weiqi turned the grips over and saw, worn into the leather, the shape of hands that were not Zhiming's.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It sets up an expected thank-you, overturns it, and explains the refusal through past events.
It describes a building's demolition and then traces the building's history from its founding.
It contrasts two men's gymnastics careers and then judges which of the two was more admirable.
It recounts a bitter argument over ownership and then shows how a third person settles it.
items.explanation: Weiqi는 감사를 기대하지만 Zhiming은 상자를 되돌려 밀어 기대가 뒤집힌다. 이어 Zhiming은 1979년 할아버지가 자신 대신 대회에 나가 그 손잡이로 우승했다는 과거를 들려주며 거절의 이유를 설명한다. 따라서 기대 제시, 반전, 과거를 통한 설명의 순서를 담은 A가 정답이다. B는 체육관의 역사를, C는 경력 비교를, D는 다툼과 중재를 다루지 않아 틀리다.

items.passage: "Play the new one," the girl at the corner table called, the moment Thuy and Somchai finished their set at the roadside diner outside Surabaya. Somchai smiled and said the new song wasn't ready yet. He had said the same thing at every stop for a month. Thuy tuned her guitar and said nothing; she had stopped asking him where the new songs were. The girl, maybe eight, frowned at him. __Then why do you always say it's almost done?__ Her mother hushed her, but the question stayed on the table like spilled tea. Somchai laughed too loudly and began packing the amplifier. Thuy watched him wind the cable around his arm, tighter and tighter, and understood that there was no new song, and perhaps had not been one for a long time.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals the girl's boredom with songs the duo has played too often.
It points out a flaw in Somchai's excuse that leads to Thuy's realization.
It shifts attention from the musicians to the girl's strict, watchful mother.
It suggests that the girl has already heard an early version of the song.
items.explanation: Somchai는 한 달 동안 모든 공연에서 새 노래가 아직 준비되지 않았다고 말해 왔다. 아이의 질문은 늘 거의 다 됐다고 하면서 왜 내놓지 않느냐는 모순을 드러내고, 이후 Somchai의 과한 웃음과 Thuy의 깨달음으로 이어진다. 따라서 변명의 허점을 짚어 Thuy의 깨달음을 이끈다는 B가 정답이다. A는 아이의 지루함으로 오해한 것이고, C와 D는 지문의 초점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: We had been in Malek's radio repair shop in Woodstock for an hour, Amara and I, and the coach still had not mentioned the anniversary. It was ten years since the club's only championship; the board wanted a ceremony in Cape Town, and Amara, benched all season, had been asked to lead the parade. She wanted to refuse. Malek, who had coached her since she was eleven, kept his hands busy on a cracked radio from the stadium's old press box. __He had repaired that same radio before every final he had ever coached.__ When it finally crackled to life, he turned the dial to the station that had called the championship and set it on the counter between them. Amara listened to the old match replaying in a broadcaster's anniversary special and, after a long while, asked him what she should wear.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Amara has been kept on the bench for the whole season.
It suggests that Malek would rather fix radios than coach the team.
It hints that Malek's repair is his indirect answer about the anniversary.
It shows that the press box radio was damaged during the championship.
items.explanation: Malek은 기념일 이야기를 꺼내지 않고 라디오만 고치는데, 밑줄 문장은 그가 결승전마다 이 라디오를 고쳐 왔다는 의식 같은 의미를 알려 준다. 이후 그는 우승을 중계한 방송을 틀어 두고, Amara는 결국 무엇을 입을지 묻는다. 두 부분을 연결하면 밑줄 문장은 수리가 기념일에 대한 Malek의 간접적인 대답임을 암시하므로 C가 정답이다. B는 그럴듯하지만 코치 일을 꺼린다는 근거가 없고, A와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.
